title: EPA 608 Type I practice test
description: Free EPA Section 608 Type I (small appliances) practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the section of 40 CFR Part 82 it comes from.

questions.question: What is the largest refrigerant charge an appliance can be factory-sealed with and still meet the definition of a small appliance?

options.C: 50 pounds
options.D: 2 pounds

questions.explanation: A small appliance is "fully manufactured, charged, and hermetically sealed in a factory with five (5) pounds or less of refrigerant." The 15-pound figure is a different limit: the largest charge on which system-dependent recovery equipment may be used.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these is named in the regulation's definition as an example of a small appliance?

options.C: An appliance holding 50 pounds of refrigerant
options.D: An under-the-counter ice maker

questions.explanation: The definition of small appliance lists examples that include dehumidifiers, vending machines, drinking water coolers and "under-the-counter ice makers." MVACs and MVAC-like appliances are handled as separate categories, and a 50-pound charge is far above the five-pound limit.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is a process stub?

options.A: A length of tubing that gives access to the refrigerant in a small appliance and can be resealed after service
options.B: A valve on a refrigerant container that seals automatically when not dispensing
options.C: The isolated portion of an appliance used to hold the refrigerant charge during service
options.D: A device that releases its refrigerant to the environment to provide cooling

questions.explanation: A process stub is "a length of tubing that provides access to the refrigerant" inside a small appliance or room air conditioner, and it can be resealed when the repair or service is done. The other options describe a self-sealing valve, a system receiver and a one-time expansion device.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A small appliance that uses a non-exempt refrigerant may not be sold unless it is equipped with what?

options.C: A process stub
options.D: A system receiver

questions.explanation: No one may sell or distribute a small appliance (other than one with only exempt refrigerants) "unless it is equipped with a process stub" to help remove refrigerant at servicing and disposal. The servicing aperture requirement applies to appliances other than small appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Using recovery equipment made on or after November 15, 1993, what recovery level does the rule set for a small appliance whose compressor is working?

options.C: 90 percent
options.D: 99 percent

questions.explanation: With equipment made on or after November 15, 1993, you must recover "90 percent of the refrigerant in the appliance when the compressor in the appliance is functioning." The 80 percent figure applies when the compressor is not working.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Using recovery equipment made on or after November 15, 1993, what recovery level does the rule set for a small appliance whose compressor is not working?

options.C: 95 percent
options.D: 50 percent

questions.explanation: With equipment made on or after November 15, 1993, the rule requires recovering 80 percent of the refrigerant "when the compressor in the appliance is not functioning." The higher 90 percent level applies only when the compressor is working.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Using recovery equipment manufactured before November 15, 1993, what recovery level does the rule set for a small appliance?

options.C: 70 percent
options.D: 80 percent

questions.explanation: When using recovery equipment manufactured before November 15, 1993, you must "recover 80 percent of the refrigerant in the small appliance." For this older equipment the rule does not set a different level based on whether the compressor works.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Instead of meeting a recovery percentage, what evacuation level does the rule set for a small appliance before it is opened or disposed of?

options.C: 5 psig
options.D: 2 inches of mercury vacuum

questions.explanation: The small appliance rule lets you meet either the recovery percentages or "evacuate the appliance to four inches of mercury vacuum." The 0 psig and 5 psig levels appear in 82.156(a), which covers appliances "except small appliances, MVACs, and MVAC-like appliances," and a 2-inch vacuum does not reach the four-inch level.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Before opening a small appliance, what kind of recovery equipment must you use?

options.A: A recovery and/or recycling machine certified under 40 CFR 82.158
options.B: Any recovery machine, as long as the technician is certified
options.C: Uncertified equipment, if the refrigerant will later be reclaimed
options.D: Uncertified equipment, if the appliance will be disposed of

questions.explanation: Before opening or disposing of a small appliance, persons must recover refrigerant "using a recovery and/or recycling machine certified pursuant to § 82.158." Technician certification, later reclamation or disposal does not replace the equipment certification requirement.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Unless it is permanently attached to the appliance as a pump-out unit, what is the largest full charge an appliance may have for system-dependent recovery equipment to be used on it?

options.C: 15 pounds
options.D: 200 pounds

questions.explanation: System-dependent equipment "may not be used with appliances with a full charge of more than 15 pounds" of refrigerant, unless it is permanently attached as a pump-out unit, so 15 pounds is the largest charge allowed. Charges of 50 or 200 pounds are over that limit, and five pounds is the small appliance limit.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What makes recovery equipment "system-dependent"?

options.A: It can remove refrigerant without help from any part of the appliance
options.B: It needs the help of components contained in the appliance to remove the refrigerant
options.C: It reprocesses refrigerant to the purity specifications in appendix A
options.D: It can only be used on motor vehicle air conditioners

questions.explanation: System-dependent recovery equipment "requires the assistance of components contained in an appliance" to remove the refrigerant. Equipment that works without that help is self-contained, and reprocessing to appendix A specifications is reclaiming.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is recovery equipment called if it can remove refrigerant from an appliance without the help of components in the appliance?

options.C: A system receiver
options.D: Self-contained recovery equipment

questions.explanation: Self-contained recovery equipment is "capable of removing the refrigerant from an appliance without the assistance of components contained in the appliance." System-dependent equipment is the opposite: it relies on the appliance's own components.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must recovery and/or recycling equipment be used?

options.A: However the technician prefers, as long as the recovery level is met
options.B: Only as described by the technician certification program
options.C: Only as described by the appliance manufacturer
options.D: According to the equipment manufacturer's directions, unless they conflict with the regulation

questions.explanation: All recovery and/or recycling equipment "must be used in accordance with the manufacturer's directions" unless those directions conflict with the requirements of the subpart. The rule points to the equipment maker's directions, not the technician's preference or the certifying program.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who must certify recovery equipment made or imported on or after November 15, 1993, for use on small appliances?

options.C: The manufacturer of the small appliance
options.D: A certified refrigerant reclaimer

questions.explanation: Equipment used on small appliances "must be certified by an approved equipment testing organization" to meet the required recovery levels. Equipment made or imported before November 15, 1993, instead "will be considered certified if it is capable" of the levels in 82.158(e)(1).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the safe disposal rule, when has the refrigerant in an appliance "leaked out"?

options.A: When someone deliberately cut the refrigerant lines
options.B: When a technician released it while removing the compressor
options.C: When it escaped because of a system failure, an accident or another unavoidable occurrence not caused by negligence
options.D: When the appliance sat unused for more than a year

questions.explanation: "Leaked out" means the refrigerant escaped "because of system failures, accidents, or other unavoidable occurrences not caused by a person's negligence or deliberate acts such as cutting refrigerant lines." If all the refrigerant leaked out, the final processor must get a signed statement saying so and that recovery is not possible.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.155, Safe disposal of appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is the passing score for a Type I certification test given in the mail-in format?

options.C: 80 percent
options.D: 90 percent

questions.explanation: Appendix D states: "The passing score for Type I certification tests using the mail-in format is 84 percent." The 70 percent score applies to the closed-book Type I, Type II, Type III and Universal tests.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Removing refrigerant in any condition from an appliance and storing it in an external container, without necessarily testing or processing it, is called what?

options.C: Recycling
options.D: Venting

questions.explanation: To recover means "to remove refrigerant in any condition from an appliance" and store it in an external container without necessarily testing or processing it. Recycling cleans the refrigerant for reuse, and reclaiming reprocesses it to the appendix A specifications.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Refrigerant recovered from a small appliance has not been recycled or reclaimed. Where may it be returned?

options.A: To the same appliance, or to another appliance owned by the same person
options.B: To any appliance, owned by anyone
options.C: Nowhere; it must always be reclaimed first
options.D: Only to a motor vehicle air conditioner

questions.explanation: Refrigerant "may be returned to the appliance from which it is recovered" or to another appliance owned by the same person without being recycled or reclaimed. This does not apply to MVACs or MVAC-like appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which certification must a person hold to maintain, service or repair small appliances?

options.C: MVAC certification under subpart B
options.D: Type I

questions.explanation: The rule states that "persons who maintain, service, or repair small appliances must be certified as Type I technicians." Type II covers medium-, high- and very high-pressure appliances, and Type III covers low-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A person disposes of small appliances but does not maintain, service or repair them. What technician certification does the rule require for that disposal work?

options.C: None; certification is not required for disposing of small appliances
options.D: Type II

questions.explanation: The rule says "persons who dispose of small appliances, MVACs, and MVAC-like appliances are not required to be certified." Type I certification is required for maintaining, servicing or repairing small appliances, not for disposing of them.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When is a registered apprentice exempt from the technician certification requirement?

options.A: When closely and continually supervised by a certified technician
options.B: When working only on appliances the apprentice owns
options.C: When working only on weekends
options.D: When the apprentice has passed a practice test

questions.explanation: Apprentices are exempt if the apprentice "is closely and continually supervised by a certified technician" during work that could release refrigerant. The supervising technician and the apprentice share responsibility for following the rules.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How long must a technician keep a copy of their certificate?

options.A: One year after passing the test
options.B: Only while working on small appliances
options.C: Until three years after no longer operating as a technician
options.D: Five years after passing the test

questions.explanation: Technicians must keep a copy of their certificate at their place of business and maintain it "until three years after no longer operating as a technician." The rule does not set a one-year or five-year period.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who is the "final processor" of a small appliance?

options.A: The technician who last serviced the appliance
options.B: The person who takes the final step in the disposal process, such as a scrap recycler or landfill operator
options.C: The company that manufactured the appliance
options.D: The reclaimer who receives the recovered refrigerant

questions.explanation: The final processor is the person who takes "the final step in the disposal process," including but not limited to scrap recyclers and landfill operators. The final processor must either recover any remaining refrigerant or verify that it was recovered.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.155, Safe disposal of appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A final processor accepts a signed statement that refrigerant was recovered from a small appliance. What must the statement include?

options.A: The serial number of the recovery machine
options.C: The weight of refrigerant recovered
options.D: The name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant, and the date it was recovered

questions.explanation: A signed statement "must include the name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant" and the date it was recovered. The rule does not list a machine serial number, certification number or refrigerant weight for this statement.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.155, Safe disposal of appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How long must the final processor of a small appliance keep the signed statements or contracts it obtains?

options.C: Until the appliance is scrapped
options.D: They do not need to be kept

questions.explanation: The final processor must keep a copy of all signed statements or contracts on site, in hard copy or electronic format, "for three years." Discarding them right away or keeping them for only one year would not meet this rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.155, Safe disposal of appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The definition of small appliance lists room air conditioners as an example. Which kind of equipment does it name as included among room air conditioners?

options.C: Packaged terminal air heat pumps
options.D: Industrial process refrigeration

questions.explanation: The definition lists "room air conditioners (including window air conditioners, portable air conditioners, and packaged terminal air heat pumps)." MVACs and MVAC-like appliances are separate categories with their own rules, and industrial process refrigeration is not named in the small appliance definition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The definition of small appliance names refrigerators and freezers designed for which uses?

options.C: Commercial use only
options.D: Military use only

questions.explanation: The definition includes "refrigerators and freezers (designed for home, commercial, or consumer use)." It is not limited to home or commercial units alone.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which refrigerant, when used in household refrigerators and freezers, is listed as exempt from the venting prohibition and the requirements of Subpart F?

options.C: HFC-134a
options.D: Isobutane (R-600a)

questions.explanation: The exempt list includes "Isobutane (R-600a) in retail food refrigerators and freezers (stand-alone units only); household refrigerators, freezers, and combination refrigerators and freezers; and vending machines." HFC-134a is not on the exempt list, so it is a non-exempt substitute, and CFC-12 and HCFC-22 are ozone-depleting refrigerants covered by the rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Propane (R-290) is exempt from the venting prohibition and the requirements of Subpart F in certain end-uses. Which of these end-uses is on that list?

options.C: MVAC-like appliances
options.D: Comfort-cooling chillers

questions.explanation: The propane exemption covers end-uses including vending machines, "self-contained commercial ice machines, very low temperature refrigeration equipment, and water coolers." Motor vehicle air conditioners, MVAC-like appliances and chillers are not in the propane list.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix D, which test formats may an organization that provides only Type I certification choose from?

options.A: Either an on-site format or a mail-in format
options.C: Only an oral format
options.D: Only a closed-book test at an EPA office

questions.explanation: Appendix D says "organizations providing Type I certification only may choose either an on-site format or a mail-in format." The program may pick either one, so it is not limited to mail-in, oral or EPA-office testing.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician paints a household refrigerator. How does the technician definition classify painting the appliance?

options.C: As an activity not reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit
options.D: As work that only a Type I technician may perform

questions.explanation: The rule says activities "such as painting the appliance, rewiring an external electrical circuit, replacing insulation on a length of pipe, or tightening nuts and bolts are not reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit." Painting does not release refrigerant, so it is not opening or disposal.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to the technician definition, activities on an appliance that has been properly evacuated under 40 CFR 82.156 are not reasonably expected to release refrigerants unless the activity includes what?

options.C: Rewiring an external electrical circuit
options.D: Adding refrigerant to the appliance

questions.explanation: Activities on properly evacuated appliances "are not reasonably expected to release refrigerants unless the activity includes adding refrigerant to the appliance." Painting, tightening nuts and bolts and rewiring an external circuit are listed as activities not expected to violate the refrigerant circuit.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix D, what must each test for Type I certification provide?

options.A: A copy of the EPA test bank
options.B: A means of verifying the identification of the individual taking the test
options.C: A list of the correct answers for self-checking
options.D: A practice version of the test

questions.explanation: Appendix D states: "Each test for Type I certification must provide a means of verifying the identification of the individual taking the test," such as a driver's license or passport. Appendix D also requires programs to keep test questions and answer keys confidential, so a test does not come with the question bank or its answers.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician recovers refrigerant from a small appliance that contains a class I or class II refrigerant or a non-exempt substitute. Under 40 CFR 82.154(b)(2), the recovery and/or recycling equipment must be certified under 40 CFR 82.158 for what?

options.A: Any one refrigerant, which then covers all others
options.B: The refrigerant only, whatever the type of appliance
options.C: MVACs only
options.D: That type of refrigerant and appliance

questions.explanation: No one may service such an appliance without "using recovery and/or recycling equipment that is certified for that type of refrigerant and appliance under § 82.158." Certification for the refrigerant alone, or for MVACs, does not meet this rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician who passed a Type I test receives a wallet-sized certification card. The card must carry a unique number for the certified person. What must that number leave out?

options.C: The name of the certifying program
options.D: The technician's name

questions.explanation: The card must include "a unique number for the certified person that does not include a technician's social security number." The card must also show the certifying program's name, the person's name and the type of certification, so those are required, not left out.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A Type I program uses the mail-in format. What deadline does Appendix D set for it to issue a certification card to a technician who passed?

options.A: No later than 60 days from the date the technician mailed the test
options.B: No later than 30 days from the date the program receives the completed test and any required documentation
options.C: No later than 90 days from the date the program receives the completed test
options.D: No later than one year from the date of the test

questions.explanation: Mail-in Type I programs "must issue cards to certified technicians no later than 30 days from the date the certifying program receives the completed test and any required documentation." The 30 days run from receipt by the program, not from when the technician mailed the test.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to the proctoring section of Appendix D, in which case is the Type I certification test a closed-book exam?

options.A: Only when it is taken by mail
options.B: Only when the technician asks for an oral test
options.C: Only when the technician is an apprentice
options.D: When it is taken as part of a Universal certification

questions.explanation: Appendix D states that the test "for Type I (if taken as part of a Universal certification), Type II, Type III, and Universal technicians is a closed-book exam." It also says "Mail-in format Type I tests cannot be used toward a Universal certification."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an in-person Type I test, what proctor ratio does Appendix D set for a certifying program?

options.A: At least one for every 10 people testing at the same time at a site
options.B: At least one for every 25 people testing at the same time at a site
options.C: At least one for every 50 people testing at the same time at a site
options.D: At least one for every 100 people testing at the same time at a site

questions.explanation: A program for "Type I (if in-person)" and the other types must designate "at least one proctor registered for every 50 people taking tests at the same time at a given site." The rule does not use a 10, 25 or 100 person ratio.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Appendix D lists the subject areas for Group II, the sector-specific questions on a Type I test. Which of these is one of them?

options.C: Changing industry outlook
options.D: Environmental impact of CFCs, HCFCs, and substitute refrigerants

questions.explanation: Group II covers sector-specific issues in "Leak detection," "Recovery Techniques," "Safety," "Shipping" and "Disposal." Laws and regulations, industry outlook and environmental impact are the Group I (core) areas.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix D, section d (Test Content), how many Group II (sector-specific) questions does a Type I certification test include?
questions.explanation: Appendix D states that "All Type I, Type II and Type III, certification tests will include 25 questions from Group I and 25 questions from Group II." The 75 Group II questions apply only to Universal tests, which have "25 from each of the three sector-specific areas."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Small-appliance recovery equipment made or imported before November 15, 1993, counts as certified if it can recover 80 percent of the refrigerant in the system under which test-stand condition?

options.A: Only with the test stand's compressor operational
options.B: Only with the test stand's compressor not operational
options.C: Whether or not the test stand's compressor is operational
options.D: Only when tested by the appliance manufacturer

questions.explanation: Equipment made or imported before that date "will be considered certified if it is capable of either recovering 80 percent of the refrigerant in the system, whether or not the compressor of the test stand is operational," or of achieving a four-inch vacuum. The split of 90 percent with the compressor operational and 80 percent when it is not is the general appendix C standard in 82.158(e).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Equipment used to evacuate a class I or class II refrigerant or a non-exempt substitute from small appliances before they are disposed of may also be certified if, tested with a properly calibrated pressure gauge, it can achieve what?

options.C: A one-inch vacuum
options.D: Recovery of 50 percent of the charge

questions.explanation: Such equipment "may also be certified if it is capable of achieving a four-inch vacuum when tested using a properly calibrated pressure gauge." The rule names a four-inch vacuum, not zero psig, a one-inch vacuum or a percentage of the charge.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Besides the certification statement, what must the label on certified small-appliance recovery equipment show?

options.C: The date the equipment was last used
options.D: The date of manufacture and the serial number (if applicable)

questions.explanation: Labels on equipment certified under 82.158(d) and (e) "must also show the date of manufacture and the serial number (if applicable) of the equipment." The rule does not ask for a technician's number, an owner's details or a date of last use on the label.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: EPA's test method for recovery devices used with small appliances (appendix C) runs its tests at what temperature?

options.A: 32 degrees F, plus or minus 2 degrees F
options.B: 75 degrees F, plus or minus 2 degrees F
options.C: 104 degrees F, plus or minus 2 degrees F
options.D: Any room temperature the laboratory chooses

questions.explanation: Appendix C states: "Tests are to be conducted at 75 degrees F, plus or minus 2 degrees F." The method sets a fixed temperature rather than leaving it to the laboratory.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix C (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these does the regulation's definition of disposal include?

options.A: Moving an appliance to a new room
options.C: Measuring an appliance's pressures with gauges
options.D: Recycling an appliance for scrap

questions.explanation: Disposal means the process leading to and including several listed activities, among them "the disassembly of any appliance for reuse of its component parts" and "the recycling of any appliance for scrap." Painting and measuring pressures are not on that list.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A final processor uses a signed contract with a supplier of small appliances instead of signed statements. What must the contract do?

options.A: List the weight of refrigerant in each appliance
options.B: Be filed with EPA within 30 days
options.C: State that the supplier will recover any remaining refrigerant before delivery, or verify that the refrigerant was properly recovered before the supplier received the appliances
options.D: Name the testing organization that certified the recovery machine

questions.explanation: A signed contract "must either state that the supplier will recover any remaining refrigerant" before delivery "or verify that the refrigerant had been properly recovered prior to receipt by the supplier." The rule does not require refrigerant weights, a filing with EPA or the name of a testing organization.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.155, Safe disposal of appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A final processor must tell its suppliers that refrigerant must be properly recovered before delivery. What form may that notice take?

options.A: Signs, letters to suppliers, or other equivalent means
options.B: Only a notice published in the Federal Register
options.C: Only a report filed with EPA
options.D: Only a notice on the technician's certification card

questions.explanation: The rule says "the form of this notification may be signs, letters to suppliers, or other equivalent means." It does not require a Federal Register notice or an EPA filing.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.155, Safe disposal of appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When is it a violation for a final processor to accept a signed statement or contract about refrigerant recovery?

options.A: When the final processor knew or had reason to know the statement or contract is false
options.B: Whenever the supplier is not a certified technician
options.C: Whenever the statement is kept in electronic format
options.D: Whenever the appliance was delivered by a third party

questions.explanation: It is a violation to accept a signed statement or contract "if the person receiving the statement or contract knew or had reason to know that the signed statement or contract is false." The rule does not tie the violation to who delivered the appliance or whether the supplier is certified, and it allows the statements to be kept "in hard copy or in electronic format."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.155, Safe disposal of appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)
